normalization.overview: A creator video positions the new Nod personal agent as a substitute for Claude Cowork. GhostMesh separates the demonstration from the operating models, vendor benchmarks, privacy flows and authorization limits.
normalization.whyItMatters: A new computer-using agent can blur product boundaries between local personal tasks, cloud agent workflows and shared business automation. Making choices requires verified outcomes, explicit cost and data-flow accounting, and permission checks at destination.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Treat Nod as a research-preview candidate for bounded personal workflows, not as proof that Cowork is obsolete. Compare the same low-risk jobs, preserve service-level authorization, and inspect actual local/provider data flows.
normalization.falsification: Matched read-only/reversible tasks against Nod and Cowork with pinned inputs, equivalent model budget, correct result, approval interventions, data flows, runtime availability and failure recovery measured.
normalization.freshness: November 11 creator walkthrough; original media privately captured and transcribed after HTTP 429. Vendor documentation supports product architecture, not a general Cowork replacement verdict.
